scores.thesis: Apple is a world-class compounder with an unmatched hardware/services ecosystem moat and exemplary capital allocation, but at ~$4.6T it is the antithesis of a micro-cap hundred-bagger candidate. Even flawless AI and services execution produces low-double-digit compounding, not 100x asymmetry.
catalysts: Services mix expansion driving margin lift
Apple Intelligence-driven iPhone upgrade cycle
Continued ~$100B/yr share repurchases
New hardware categories (Vision line, home/robotics optionality)
risks: Law of large numbers caps upside from $4.6T base
Antitrust pressure on App Store take rate and Google TAC payments
China demand softness and supply-chain concentration
AI execution lag versus hyperscaler peers
scores.pass_reason: ~$4.6T mega-cap; a 100x implies a ~$457T valuation exceeding global GDP. Superb business, wrong mandate for a hundred-bagger satellite sleeve.

scores.thesis: Microsoft combines durable enterprise moats with leading AI positioning via Azure and Copilot, with strong returns on capital and disciplined allocation. At ~$3.7T, however, the asymmetry required for a hundred-bagger simply does not exist; this is a core compounder, not a satellite moonshot.
catalysts: Azure AI revenue acceleration
Copilot enterprise seat monetization
OpenAI partnership economics and model integration
Operating leverage after AI capex wave normalizes
risks: AI capex intensity pressuring free cash flow margins
Uncertainty on enterprise AI ROI and Copilot attach rates
Regulatory/antitrust overhang on bundling and OpenAI ties
Valuation multiple already reflects AI leadership
scores.pass_reason: ~$3.7T mega-cap; 100x implies ~$370T. Core-holding quality, but categorically outside the hundred-bagger satellite mandate.

scores.thesis: Berkshire is a fortress balance sheet with elite capital allocation and a diversified collection of high-return operating businesses plus a massive equity portfolio. But at ~$1T market cap, even Buffett-descendant excellence compounds at market-beating—not hundred-bagger—rates. Fails the mandate on size alone.
catalysts: Deployment of ~$300B+ cash pile into a market dislocation
Insurance float and underwriting profit growth
BNSF and Berkshire Hathaway Energy earnings expansion
Continued buybacks when trading below intrinsic value
risks: Post-Buffett succession and key-person transition
Size drag: too big to move the needle with new investments
Insurance catastrophe loss exposure
Equity portfolio concentration (notably Apple)
scores.pass_reason: ~$1T conglomerate with the greatest capital allocator in history, but size is the anchor on returns; a 100x outcome is arithmetically implausible.

scores.thesis: AST SpaceMobile is building the first space-based cellular broadband network connecting directly to unmodified smartphones—a genuinely massive TAM spanning billions of mobile users—with blue-chip validation from AT&T, Verizon, Vodafone, Rakuten, and Google. The moat is a patent/wholesale-MNO model plus first-mover constellation scale. At ~$28B, though, the market has priced in significant success: the sub-$2B hundred-bagger entry window has closed, leaving credible multi-bagger rather than 100x potential.
catalysts: Commercial service activation with MNO partners
BlueBird Block 2 satellite launches and constellation buildout
New MNO, government, and defense contract awards
Regulatory/spectrum coordination milestones and path to FCF breakeven
risks: Heavy ongoing capex and recurring equity dilution
Launch and satellite deployment execution risk
SpaceX Starlink direct-to-cell competition
Spectrum/regulatory risk
Valuation already discounts substantial multi-year success

scores.thesis: Rocket Lab is the clear Western #2 in launch with a genuinely integrated Space Systems segment and a credible Neutron medium-lift rocket, led by exceptional founder-operator Peter Beck with a strong execution record. The end-to-end space company model is a real moat. However, at ~$50B the valuation capitalizes years of flawless execution—a 100x implies ~$5T, which is not credible—so it fails the hundred-bagger mandate despite high business quality.
catalysts: Neutron first launch and reusability milestones
Space Systems backlog growth (satellite buses, components, constellation wins)
National security awards (HASTE, NSSL Phase 3 eligibility)
Record Electron launch cadence
risks: Neutron development delays, cost overruns, or failure
Negative margins and continued cash burn
SpaceX rideshare economics compressing small-launch pricing
Extreme price-to-sales multiple vulnerable to any slip

scores.thesis: Intuitive Machines is the leading pure-play on the NASA-funded lunar economy, with CLPS delivery contracts, NSNS lunar communications services, and first-mover heritage from the first commercial Moon landing. At ~$3.6B it is among the smaller caps here, so a 10x+ outcome is conceivable if the lunar cislunar economy materializes. But revenue is lumpy, each mission carries binary risk, and 100x requires a $350B+ lunar-infrastructure company—speculative even in bull scenarios.
catalysts: IM-3/IM-4 mission execution and additional CLPS awards
Near Space Network Services (lunar data relay) revenue ramp
Lunar Terrain Vehicle and cargo delivery awards
Emerging commercial and allied-nation lunar payload demand
risks: Binary mission failure risk on each landing
Dependence on NASA budget cycles and contract timing
Dilution and working-capital strain between milestone payments
Small float, high volatility, and lumpy revenue recognition

scores.thesis: Redwire is a diversified space-infrastructure consolidator with real revenue, a broad component portfolio (solar arrays, sensors, in-space manufacturing), and an expanding defense footprint via Edge Autonomy. It is the best mandate fit in this universe: smallest cap, tangible unit economics, and a roll-up strategy echoing proven aerospace compounders. Still, 100x from ~$3.2B implies a $320B company—implausible—so it screens as a quality multi-bagger, not a hundred-bagger.
catalysts: Edge Autonomy integration expanding defense revenue and margins
Backlog conversion in solar arrays, antennas, and digital engineering
Further accretive bolt-on M&A in space infrastructure
National security space budget tailwinds (SDA, missile tracking constellations)
risks: Integration and leverage risk from serial acquisitions
Government contract concentration and budget timing
Thin GAAP profitability and competitive pricing pressure
100x outcome ($320B+) far beyond any credible space-infrastructure scenario

scores.thesis: SoundHound has real voice-AI traction across restaurant ordering and automotive assistants with triple-digit growth and a broadened platform via the Amelia acquisition. The moat question is severe, however: hyperscalers and LLM-native competitors are converging on the same use cases, gross margins are pressured, and losses remain large. At ~$3.5B and a rich sales multiple, risk/reward is skewed against the asymmetric profile the mandate requires.
catalysts: Restaurant drive-thru and phone-ordering rollouts at scale
Automotive generative-AI voice assistant design wins
Amelia cross-sell into enterprise customer-service automation
Path to adjusted EBITDA breakeven
risks: Competition from OpenAI, Google, and Amazon voice/LLM stacks
Persistent GAAP losses and shareholder dilution
Customer concentration and long enterprise sales cycles
High short interest and extreme valuation volatility

scores.thesis: IonQ's trapped-ion architecture offers high-fidelity qubits and a credible technical roadmap toward networked quantum systems, and quantum computing is an enormous option-value TAM. But the stock is effectively a long-dated call option: revenue is in the tens of millions against an ~$18B market cap. The 100x window closed when the market pre-paid for the quantum future; multiple-compression risk now dominates the asymmetry.
catalysts: New system launches and algorithmic-qubit milestones
Government and enterprise quantum computing contracts
Quantum networking progress via photonic interconnects
Demonstrations approaching quantum advantage
risks: Revenue in the tens of millions versus ~$18B valuation
Heavy dilution funding decades-long roadmap
Fault-tolerant timelines could slip many years
Competition from IBM, Google, Quantinuum, and well-funded private peers
Hype-cycle drawdown risk and insider selling

scores.thesis: Joby leads the eVTOL certification race with deep partners (Toyota, Delta) and a first-mover commercial path in Dubai, targeting a genuinely novel urban air mobility market. It remains pre-scale with heavy cash burn and unproven unit economics, and the ~$8.5B valuation already prices certification success. Hundred-bagger math (~$850B) is not plausible; downside on any certification slip is severe.
catalysts: FAA type certification progression through final stages
Dubai commercial air-taxi launch
US market entry (NYC/LA) with Delta partnership
Toyota-backed manufacturing scale-up and DoD logistics contracts
risks: Certification delays and sustained heavy cash burn
Unit economics unproven at commercial cadence; vertiport infrastructure unbuilt
Competition from Archer, Wisk, Vertical, and Chinese eVTOL OEMs
Regulatory and public-acceptance risk for urban air mobility
